title: Graded Phase Hours for Work Conditioning and Work Hardening Program Days
content:
# Graded phase hours

Program days in the Work Conditioning Program and the Work Hardening Program of the Workers' Compensation Referral are graded by phase. The graded phase hours of a day follow the progression day count of that day. The count is kept in calendar days; where it is reckoned from the initial evaluation, the initial evaluation is the date of service of the referral's evaluation charge.

**Phase schedule.** While the progression day count is under fourteen (14) days, the graded phase hours are the program's minimum daily program hours. From fourteen to twenty-seven days they are the midpoint of the program's minimum and maximum daily program hours, rounded down to a whole hour. From twenty-eight (28) days on they are the program's maximum daily program hours.

| Progression day count | Phase | Graded phase hours |
|---|---|---|
| 0 to 13 days | opening phase | the program's minimum daily program hours |
| 14 to 27 days | middle phase | the midpoint of the minimum and maximum daily program hours, rounded down to a whole hour |
| 28 days or more | full phase | the program's maximum daily program hours |

## The figures for each program

| Program | Minimum daily program hours | Midpoint, rounded down | Maximum daily program hours |
|---|---|---|---|
| Work Conditioning Program | 2 | 3 | 4 |
| Work Hardening Program | 4 | 6 | 8 |

The midpoint is half of the minimum and maximum taken together: half of 2 and 4 together is 3; half of 4 and 8 together is 6. Where that half falls between whole hours it is rounded down; for a hypothetical program with a minimum of 3 and a maximum of 6 daily hours, half of 9 is 4.5, recorded as 4.

## Edges of the phases

- Day 13 is still the opening phase; day 14 opens the middle phase.
- Day 27 is still the middle phase; day 28 opens the full phase.
